_doc: The reward the AI learns from. One weight per event; the reward of a decision is the sum of weight x event.

Edit the numbers, keep the names. Most terms are game events (src/core/game.ts, Events), counted once per decision (4 ticks = 1/15 s). meters, moves, reversals and pointlessJumpsRolls are computed in train/runner_env.py.
Every term is also logged on its own (reward/<name>), so the dashboard shows which part drives learning.
The benchmark never uses this file: it scores with the game's own score (metres + 5 per coin).
Scale: one second of running earns about +1 to +2 (10-20 m/s x 0.1 per metre). The wasted-move costs (-0.02) are 1-2 % of that, so dodging always pays more.

meters.doc: per metre moved forward this decision (from the game's distance in mm). The main signal: survive and go far.

coins.doc: per coin picked up. Off at first: coin greed makes it take risky lanes.

jumps.doc: per jump started. Make it slightly negative if it learns to spam jumps.

rolls.doc: per roll started. Make it slightly negative if it learns to spam rolls.

laneChanges.doc: per lane change. Slightly negative stops left-right jitter.

stumbles.doc: per side hit (the first one only bounces you back; the second within 5 s kills).

died.doc: once, when the run ends in a crash.

moves.doc: per decision with an action other than nothing (left, right, jump, roll), whether or not it did anything. A small cost makes it act only when needed.

reversals.doc: per lane change that undoes the previous one within 8 decisions (0.53 s): left then right, or right then left. Targets jitter.

pointlessJumpsRolls.doc: per jump or roll started with no obstacle ahead in its lane within 12 m (about the length of one jump at top speed). Coins and power-ups do not count as obstacles.
